text:
inc-bot: paging devon_oncall (severity: P1) — embedding endpoints showing sustained fanout from unknown proxies, error rate spiking 35% and tail latency > 5s for customers in APAC. Auto-run started: collect stack traces + request samples

sara.k: I see a flood of small embedding requests with identical prompt hashes, high K/V churn. Looks like a scraper farm.

mike-r: confirmed ASN clusters from several cloud providers, most requests hitting /v1/embeddings/batch with tiny batch_size=1.

anna_ops: are we seeing rate limit tripped for customers? which tier affected?

devon_oncall: enterprise customers fine, self-serve free tier showing elevated errors and throttles. Impact: increased 503s and some quota exhaustion alerts.

nina_s: WAF signals show repetitive UA fingerprints and missing referer. Recommend immediate geo-rate-slice for APAC and block signatures hitting 200+ r/s per IP.

kevin_sec: propose temporary WAF rule to block the top 3 offending ASNs + enable challenge for suspicious IPs. also rotate the API gateway token used by internal metrics ingestion.

sara.k: on the runtime side I can disable embeddings batching for 5m to reduce KV cache churn and force per-request cost accounting. That should slow throughput but stabilize latency.

devon_oncall: do it. I'll also set a dynamic quota: per-key embedding QPS cap = 5 for free tiers, 50 for paid, effective immediately.

mike-r: deploying rate-slice: edge policy change queued. curl snippet to trigger deploy (ops only):
```
POST /edge/policies/slice
{ "region":"apac","limit":5,"scope":"free" }
```

deploy-bot: change accepted — edge policy update initiated in eu-sg-1, apac-tok-1. Expected propagation 30s.

devon_oncall: WAF rule rolled out to block ASN 136.243.0.0/16 and 45.77.0.0/16. Monitoring.

nina_s: captcha challenge enabled for requests with empty referer and UA containing "curl|python-requests".

sara.k: embeddings batching disabled on pool-e2 for 10m to let KV cache settle. Observability note: token throughput will spike; costs may increase temporarily.

mike-r: starting sampling job to pull full headers for 10k requests to help fingerprinting. storing in /incidents/3712345678/samples (access: sec-team).

kevin_sec: customer comms draft: "We are mitigating bot-driven traffic that impacted embedding latency. We've applied temporary rate limits and WAF rules; paid customers not expected to be impacted. We'll follow up with post-incident analysis." Approve?

anna_ops: approve, add a line about potential short-term increase in token usage and cost for some users.

devon_oncall: handoff note — if spike persists after 30m, escalate to infra to spin a temporary dedicated embedding pool and enable model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model. Next oncall: @mike-r.

mike-r: ack. I'll monitor for 45m then either scale pool or reopen rate caps.

inc-bot: automation: incident ticket created INC-2026-3712345678. Pager cleared for devon_oncall at 2026-03-17T09:42:58Z.

sara.k: early metrics: error rate down from 35% -> 6% in APAC, p95 latency down from 5.1s -> 1.2s. continuing monitoring.

kevin_sec: leaving notes: saved WAF rule id waf-emb-proxy-3712, edge policy id slice-apac-3712. retain logs for 90 days.

devon_oncall: moving to watch. If anything pops, DM page. Good job team :thumbsup:

mike-r: will follow up with postmortem template and customer impact numbers once we have full logs.

deploy-bot: edge policy propagation complete in apac regions.

inc-bot: incident status -> mitigated; keep open for RCA.

anna_ops: leaving customer support a note to prepare for 2-3 inbound tickets about throttling. Template: "We applied temporary rate limits to mitigate bot traffic; paid customers should not be affected. If you see degraded performance, please share request id and region."

sara.k: tagging this for model-team to consider detection rules at model-call layer (identify small identical prompt hashes).

devon_oncall: final: handoff to normal ops at 10:30Z, assign RCA to sara.k and mike-r. Closing page.
